title: Stream probe negotiation and idempotent replay for resilient tool-invocation boundaries
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Implement a client/server probe-and-handshake flow to improve reconnect behavior for streaming responses, preserve tool-invocation (tool/function) boundaries across reconnects, and provide an idempotent replay mechanism that is compatible with legacy SSE clients. This ticket scopes the protocol additions, runtime changes (server-side checkpointing and dedupe), client hints for upgrade, and a compatibility shim for older HTTP/1.1 eventstream consumers.
acceptance_criteria: New Stream-Proto handshake header is negotiated when client sends X-RI-Stream-Proto: 2 and server responds with Accept-RI-Stream: 2
Server can issue ephemeral checkpoint hints (checkpoint_id + seq_range) every N tokens and persist them to the request trace store
Client reconnect using last checkpoint replays only missing sequence range; server performs idempotent dedupe using (session_id, checkpoint_id, chunk_fingerprint) and returns clear resume status
Tool-invocation boundaries are never split across resumable-replay windows; the runtime defers commit of a tool-invocation until chunk with boundary marker is persisted
Compatibility shim: if client omits X-RI-Stream-Proto, server falls back to sentinel event framing using 'ri-compat' events and a short-lived resume token in HTTP headers
E2E smoke tests (unit + integration) validate reconnect, replay, and tool-invocation semantics under packet loss and 20% reconnect churn
Load test (k=1k concurrent streams) shows <5% P95 latency regression vs baseline and <2x token duplication rate during reconnect scenarios
tasks: Define handshake: headers, probe frame, TTL, and version negotiation
Implement server-side ephemeral checkpoint hints and persist to trace store
Add dedupe layer keyed by (session_id, epoch, chunk_hash)
Mark and atomicize tool-invocations so replay does not re-execute side effects
Implement client-side reconnect logic that prefers probe+resume and falls back to compat shim
Create compatibility shim that emits 'ri-compat' sentinel events and short resume tokens for legacy clients
Add integration tests and run load tests; record results in dashboard
comments: 2025-01-15 Marco Ruiz: Kickoff — scoped handshake proto and initial prototyping plan. Will reuse parts of trace-store interface introduced in ENG-142111.

2025-01-21 Design review: Decided on dual-path approach: explicit Stream-Proto v2 handshake for upgraded clients, and a lightweight sentinel-event shim for legacy SSE consumers. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STREAM/Probe+Handshake+v2

2025-01-24 Engineering note: Chose checkpoint cadence of ~512 tokens by default; adjustable via X-RI-Checkpoint-Interval header. Trade-off: more frequent checkpoints reduce replay size but increase metadata write rate.
2025-01-28 Security review request submitted (PR #2384) — needs explicit review for resume tokens stored in trace logs. See security notes in the doc.
2025-01-30 Load test (canary infra) showed 1.8x write amplification to trace store at default cadence; we will optimize by batching checkpoint writes in ENG-147000.

2025-02-02 QA: Integration tests for tool-invocation boundary preservation failing when chunk size > 8KB. Root cause: the runtime was emitting boundary marker only at tokenizer flush events; patch submitted in PR #2410.
2025-02-03 Marco Ruiz: Updated implementation notes and landed minimal server handshake. Client lib patch pending review (SDK PR #1197).
implementation_notes: Key design: session_id assigned at request start; handshake introduces a monotonic epoch that increments when server rolls the session or when model variant changes. Checkpoint message contains {checkpoint_id, epoch, last_seq, fingerprint_window}. On reconnect client provides last_seq and preferred_checkpoint_id; server computes missing ranges and replies with resume_status = {ok|stale|full-replay}.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: resume tokens leaking in long-term logs. Mitigation: redact tokens in long-term retention and rotate token format every 24h. Risk: double-execute tool-invocations during replay. Mitigation: runtime will mark invocation as 'tentative' until checkpoint commit and use idempotency key for downstream calls.
next_steps: Finish client SDK changes, complete security review, run full-scale chaos reconnect tests (k=10k streams), and roll out as opt-in behind X-RI-Stream-Proto: 2. After opt-in validation, flip default in runtime-1.24.
